definitions.gloss: various circumstances; various reasons; a number of factors
definitions.explanation: Refers to multiple reasons or circumstances, often used when the speaker does not wish to specify the exact details.

examples.japanese: {諸事情|しょじじょう}により{中止|ちゅうし}します。
examples.english: It will be canceled due to various circumstances.

examples.japanese: {諸事情|しょじじょう}があって{参加|さんか}できません。
examples.english: I can't participate due to various reasons.

examples.japanese: {諸事情|しょじじょう}を{考慮|こうりょ}した{結果|けっか}、{計画|けいかく}を{変更|へんこう}することになった。
examples.english: As a result of considering various circumstances, it was decided to change the plan.

notes:
Composed of {諸|しょ} (various, many) + {事情|じじょう} (circumstances, reasons). This word is commonly used in formal or semi-formal contexts when the speaker wants to cite reasons without going into specifics.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {諸事情|しょじじょう}により: due to various circumstances
- {諸事情|しょじじょう}があって: because of various reasons
- {諸事情|しょじじょう}を{考慮|こうりょ}して: taking various circumstances into account
- {諸事情|しょじじょう}から: from various circumstances

USAGE:
Often functions as a polite way to avoid giving a specific reason. In announcements, it serves as a catch-all explanation for cancellations, delays, or changes. In everyday speech, it can be a tactful way to decline an invitation or explain a decision without revealing personal details.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {事情|じじょう}: circumstances — singular or general; {諸事情|しょじじょう} emphasizes that there are multiple factors
- {都合|つごう}: convenience/circumstances — more personal and informal
